chapter: Trumpeters he admired and the Ellington near-miss
title: Freddie Jenkins and the Christmas War Bonds from Cab's band
summary: Cab and Duke were booked by the same office and Cab's band chipped in every Christmas to send ailing Freddie Jenkins, in hospital with TB, a War Bond; Jones was glad to hear he was back.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Yeah. He was something else. The thing about it, we always thought of Duke as a sister band, you know, to Cab.
Yeah.

And so -- because we was booked out of the same office, and in fact once there was only the two bands out of the office. My agent now is Sam Burke. He was booking with Duke and Cab and left Mills by that time, you know. And Mitlow was the head man to keep the stuff together.
Yes.

And so Freddie got sick, and to show you the kinds of hearts guys had back in those days, we would get together every year, around about Christmas time, and put in a little money apiece, you know, everybody --
Both bands.
Well, our band did. I don't know about Duke, but we did.
No, I never heard of it before.
No, but we did it. Our band did it. Cab's band did it, and we'd send -- get a War Bond -- see, it was during wartime.
Yeah.
And we'd send Freddie Jenkins a War Bond every year.
Wasn't that nice. That was very nice.
It wasn't much, but it was something. He was in the hospital, you know.
Well, it was very nice, and it must have moved him, you know.
Sure, to let him know that somebody was out here thinking about him.
That's right.
Because he stayed there quite awhile, I think, with that TB he had, I think.
Yeah. He was sick a long while.

And I was so glad to hear that he's back, because I missed him. I heard at one time that he was a disc jockey in Dallas, and we played there last year, in '77, so I figured maybe we'd get to see him, but I inquired about him and nobody knew, and we didn't have long to inquire, you know.
Well, you know, I think he was in Ft. Worth, which is what, like half an hour away, 40 minutes away or something like that?
Yeah, about that.
And I suppose maybe he hadn't come around.
